messages:
kai: FYI I opened a perf thread — seeing weird tail-latency sawtooth on Llama-3-13b after the rope_theta default drift. profiler shows repeated kernel selector flips + small KV cache thrash. anyone else?

ben: saw a few anomalies on canary yesterday, but thought it was noisy infra. can you paste the trace?

kai: pasting the hot slice (trimmed):
```
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z pid=4312 hotkernels: select_kernel(arch=llama3, seq=512, head_dim=128) -> xformer_rotary_fast
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z pid=4312 hotkernels: select_kernel(arch=llama3, seq=8, head_dim=128) -> fallback_pointwise
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z pid=4312 kvcache: evict(approx) depth=2 reason=batch_boundary
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z pid=4312 latency: p99=265ms p50=22ms
```
kai: note the rapid kernel switch at different seq lengths inside the same mini-batch — looks like our batching heuristic is interleaving long and short sequences and then kernel selection flips back and forth.

sara: that kernel flip is expensive because we rebind workspace and call different launch configs. add hysteresis to the selector? e.g., stick to a chosen kernel for a micro-window unless >20% perf penalty.

ben: +1 hysteresis. Also the KV cache eviction on batch_boundary looks suspicious. are we treating prefix cached contexts as eligible for eviction prematurely?

ana: (perf-bot) Attached heap and kernel usage snapshot for run 2026-03-12-09:12. Looks like head_dim 128 + rope_theta=320 leads to kernel mismatch between "rotary_fast" and "rotary_generic" for seqs < 16.

kai: here's the minimal repro config I used:
```json
{
  "model": "llama-3-13b",
  "rope_theta": 320,
  "head_dim": 128,
  "batching": {
    "max_items": 32,
    "seq_grouping": "by_arrival",
    "short_seq_threshold": 16
  }
}
```

kai: observed behavior: when a long seq (512) arrives after a burst of small seqs, selector oscillates, KV gets partially evicted to free workspace, then cold cache misses blow up p99.

sara: can you try forcing `seq_grouping: by_size` to avoid interleaving? If that reduces oscillation it's definitely batching policy causing it.

kai: tried `by_size` — p99 stable ~120ms, but throughput drops ~8%. so tradeoff. Would prefer selector-level fix + tiny batching tweak.

ben: idea: add two fixes together: 1) selector hysteresis (stick for N tokens or M ms), 2) KV pinning for active contexts in last-k batches (don't evict unless memory pressure > 95%). That should avoid repeated rebuilds + keep throughput.

ana: also check RMSNorm vs SiLU pathing for the same model variant. Our autotuner picks a different fused kernel when SiLU is on; combined with rope_theta boundary it increases register pressure causing kernel to fall back. Might be triple-interaction: nonlinear activation -> different kernel -> head dim register usage -> fallback on small seqs.

kai: ugh. we should run an ablation where we flip SiLU->GELU and rope_theta values across head_dim variants. small matrix of runs: rope=256/320/384 x head_dim=64/128 x activation=SiLU/GELU. I'll kick that off on dedicated-reserve.

ben: log an experiment ticket + link results. Also add a short-term quick guard: if selector would switch kernel within the same batch across >10% of items, prefer the kernel with lower worst-case p99. (conservative choice)

kai: created ticket: https://rwinf.atlassian/EXP-1723 — added config + initial traces. Leaving notes for oncall: avoid global rope_theta changes mid-rollout; roll per-model.

ana: one more note — chat-template inference tends to produce many short seqs followed by occasional long streaming continuation. For chat workloads, default `short_seq_threshold` should be raised so short/long mixing is less likely.

ben: agreed. let's add a runtime flag `batching.allow_interleave=false` for chat templates by default.

kai: TL;DR: repro confirmed, root cause = batching interleave + selector hysteresis missing + KV eviction too eager. Plan: add selector hysteresis, KV pinning threshold, tweak chat defaults, run ablation matrix. I'll post perf numbers when experiments finish. :+1:

sara: thanks. if you need help with kernel binding code I can pair this week.

ben: happy to review the autotuner heuristic PR.

kai: thanks — will assign reviews when PRs are up.
